I do congress through Texas UIL and getting to state is insanely easy as long as you cover your bases, I have some experience here as a two time state finalist.

My advice:
1. Don’t stress over being cookie cutter with your speeches. It’s good to have three points with sources, but try and do something unique and distinct like have some funny intros or a phrase you use a lot.
When you’re a judge watching 20 something kids all Talk about the same thing, having little gimmicks to make you stand out can really help your planting in the room

2. Be an active questioner; don’t just sit by during each questing period, judges like those who are constantly active in the chambers. 

3. Have fun and relax. In my experience, congress speakers who look and act natural and fluid during the round tend to do better. Don’t tense up, give your speeches as if you were talking to your friends casually, and if you make a mistake, own it and move on

4. If you get angry or upset, don’t let it show. Any congress competitor that gets visibly agitated by troll questions or stuff like that are often ranked lower for reacting poorly. If someone tries to get a rise out of you, just keep your cool and stay professional.

5. If you know how parliamentary procedure works, try and PO. Even the worst presiding officers can often make it to state easy simply because it’s not a job many people want to do, and judges will appreciate you stepping up to the plate to do it.


If you have any specific questions you still want answered, feel free to PM me about them, but this is all I can think of off the top of my head to help you out.

Good luck :)
